subject: 0112 reservation: usage Q&A for render/encode (retire seq, 200 ms rule, limits, fallback)
body:
0112 surface reservation: usage notes and answers for the render lead / encode (kernel side is final in the repo: gpu/include/nord2_gpu_transport.h has NORD2_GPU_SEL_SURFACE_RESERVE 13, NORD2_GPU_SEL_SURFACE_RETIRE 14, NORD2_GPU_RESERVE_MAX 8; device images P14/P15 carry it; README gpu/build/kernel-p1-20261026/README-0112.md). Ask here if anything below is not what you need.
1. When does a reserved surface stop being busy? RETIRE(R, seq) with seq = id of the LAST SUBMIT_JM of the frame in the SAME context: busy until every job of that context with id <= seq is terminal (done, faulted -> verified stop/reset, cancelled, reset). Order does not matter: retiring after the jobs finished (even after WAIT_SEQ reaped them) releases at once; retiring before they finish keeps busy until they end. seq must be an id the kernel has issued (otherwise BadArgument and the reservation stays).
2. Frame that is not going to be submitted (encode failed, empty frame, drop): RETIRE(R, 0) cancels immediately. Process death or context close drops all reservations of that context; a GPU reset drops all of them.
3. 200 ms rule: an UNRETIRED reservation older than 200 ms stops counting as busy (counted in resv_expired, shown in NORD2 FB PRESENT as resv_expired=N and in the JOBS line as resv=reserves/retires/cancels/expired). There is no renew selector. If an encode+submit can take longer than 200 ms (blur-heavy frames?) tell me: the cheap fix is a RENEW (refresh the timestamp, same R) or a longer window for the first reservation; both are ~20 lines in the core plus tests. Until then do not rely on a reservation older than 200 ms, and treat RETIRE returning NotFound as "it already expired".
4. Limits: at most 8 surfaces per reservation, at most 4 live reservations per context (5th returns Busy and R=0: fall back to scheduled-after-last-submit for that frame), 32 overall. Handles must be this context's IMPORT_SURFACE handles; two handles to the same IOSurface name the same surface. A buffer that is not an imported surface, an unknown handle or another context's handle gives BadArgument. RESERVE does not hold the buffers: you may release the import before RETIRE (the reservation only remembers which surface).
5. Probe/kill switch: RESERVE with n = 0 answers success with R = 0 (no side effect); under the boot-arg n2resv=0 (image ui654fb60noresv) BOTH selectors including the n = 0 probe return kIOReturnUnsupported, so treat any probe result other than {success, R=0} as "not available" and keep the old path. On pre-0112 kernels the selector is unknown: also not {success, R=0}.
6. What the kernel does with it: nord2_gpu_surface_busy(S) is true for a reserved S (same lock as the job-based check, for every client and for the vsync handler); a swap that finds S busy is requeued by the 0102 logic for at most 6 ticks, then forced (busy_forced). So releasing CA at hand-off is safe exactly as long as RESERVE returned before you report scheduled, and the frame's last job is submitted and RETIREd inside 200 ms (or cancelled).
7. Chaining (C6q): one RETIRE with the seq of the last job of the chain covers every job up to it. If one reservation covers K frames' surfaces, retire once at the chain's last id.
8. Include order: gpu/metal/tegu/nord2_transport.inc defines the trap block that gpu/include/nord2_gpu_transport.h also defines (since 0111). Include the .inc first (as compute_frontend.m does); since 0113 the header yields to it (the frontend API-surface host test needed that).
9. On-device check once used: JOBS resv=r/t/c/e should show r == t + c, e == 0 in steady state; resv_expired=0 in FB PRESENT. e > 0 means frames were reserved but never retired within 200 ms.
